thread:
emma: quick follow-up to the loader consolidation discussion. proposal: one multiplexing loader that handles transports (s3/http/sidecar) and formats (safetensors, pt, tar+chunks) with a tiny, strictly-bounded sync hotpath to get inference started, then async hydrates rest of the tensors. sketch below.

jorge: agree on single surface, but big caution: we must enforce time/IO bounds on the sync hotpath. otherwise callers will see unpredictable tails. we should specify a strict contract: sync path returns only 'seed' layers + metadata and a handle. anything else is async.

lia: suggested minimal ABI to implement this sprint:
```
// blocking, bounded (e.g. < 200ms)
LoadSync(model_ref, seed_policy) -> {handle, fast_meta, seed_blob(s)}

// non-blocking, background continuation
Hydrate(handle, hydrate_policy) -> immediately returns, emits events
```
seed_policy defaults to [token-embed, first-2-blocks], hydrate_policy includes {credit_budget, parity, quant_goal}.

arjun: +1 but credit_budget must be per-model-instance/request-group, not global. otherwise a large warmup job will starve small latency requests. also need a runtime backpressure hook: runtime should send pressure_level and desired_latency_SLO so loader can downgrade (replicate -> striped) or pick pre-quantized artifacts.

emma: agree. runtime-bot: note event schema "loader.pressure" posted. loader should adapt prefetch aggressiveness based on pressure and policy.

jorge: operational tradeoff: on-the-fly quantization during hydration saves storage and shipping cost but may blow CPU/GPU during canary. gate dynamic-quant behind deployment tier: hosted -> prefer pre-quantized; dedicated -> allow dynamic with limits.

lia: on shard resolution: manifest v2 should include canonical chunk ids and CA blobs. loader needs ResolveChunk(chunk_id) -> [uris] + prefer_local hint. add small LRU for resolves. allow an override for on-prem to force local copy.

arjun: also support dedup_key for blobs shared across models (e.g., same embedding). dedup_key = content_hash + origin_ns. transport layer can cache by dedup_key to avoid duplicate downloads.

emma: failure modes: if chunk download fails mid-hydration: 1) emit telemetry, 2) retry alternates, 3) if non-critical chunk skip and serve degraded, if critical fail-fast. ops: runbook?

ops: runbook draft: on chunk failure mark model instance as degraded, route new traffic to fallback variant if configured, schedule manifest integrity check. fire alert after repeated failures (>= 5min or >3 distinct chunks). include degraded_reason tag in metrics. keep noise low.

lia: events we should emit (compact):
```
loader.hydration.started {handle, model_ref, seed_layers}
loader.hydration.progress {handle, chunk_id, bytes, transport}
loader.hydration.failed {handle, chunk_id, error, attempts}
loader.loadsync.latency {handle, ms}
```
lightweight and aggregated.

jorge: testing: unit tests for ResolveChunk and LoadSync boundedness (simulate slow/failing transports), integration test with a fake transport that aborts mid-stream, e2e perf for cold-start (sync only) and steady-state token cost accounting for background hydration.

arjun: migration: land behind feature-flag. enable for internal canary and a tiny percentage of hosted traffic. auto-fallback if LoadSync exceeds X ms or Hydrate error rate > Y% in first N minutes.

emma: action items: lia to open ABI PR + mocked transport tests; jorge to draft credit_budget semantics + simulator for credit vs tail-latency; arjun to prototype dedup_key caching in sidecar transport; ops to produce runbook snippet and alert thresholds. i'll fold into RFC addendum.

lia: I'll open the PR today, include the minimal manifest-v2 shim and a small fake transport for tests. cc @emma @jorge

jorge: I'll add a short note about pre-quantization defaults per deployment tier and a few sim numbers.

runtime-bot: deploy-bot: planned canary enable window requested: 2024-11-12 08:00-12:00 UTC.

emma: sounds good. this scope is feasible for next sprint. :rocket:
